claims.text: The documented half is unusually specific. Qwen's launch post gives the model's shape in a single clause: "2.4T parameters (95B active), with open weights releasing next week" [^1].
Alongside the $2/$6 base, QwenCloud publishes an implicit cache read at $0.25, an explicit cache *creation* charge at $2.50, and an explicit cache read at $0.17 [^2].
A 991K maximum input plus a 131K maximum output exceeds the 1M window, so these are per-field ceilings, not a budget you can spend simultaneously [^2].

Artificial Analysis measures Qwen3.8-Max at a blended $1.18 per million tokens — cheaper than its own card implies, because input dominates real traffic — and simultaneously at $2,159.51 to complete the Intelligence Index, having burned 150M output tokens against a comparison median of 63M, with the model explicitly labelled "very verbose" [^10].
Independently, Artificial Analysis places the served model at Intelligence Index 53, ranked #16 of 186, at 46.5 output tokens/sec, ranked #122 of 186 [^10].
The row Alibaba's messaging leans hardest on is Terminal-Bench 2.1, where 86.6 beats both Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Fable 5 at 84.6 — and still trails GPT-5.6 Sol at 88.8 [^1][^21].

Analysts reconstructing the comparison report that the competitor columns were not re-run under those conditions — Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 appear under Terminus 2 via Artificial Analysis, GPT-5.6 Sol under Codex [^21].

How much does that matter? Independent work measuring the same models across harnesses puts GPT-5.5 at 82.7 under Codex CLI and 53.5 under Terminus-2, a 29.2-point swing attributable to scaffold alone; DeepSeek-V4-Pro moves 67.9 to 50.0 on the same axis [^23].
By 2.0 points, measured on a different harness than its rivals. Harness choice alone moves the same benchmark by up to 29.2 points [^1][^23].

Qwen's WideSearch footnote states the setup outright — "Claude Code harness for external models and the Qwen-Agent harness for ours" — and its Fable 5 column carries the caveat that "Fable5 results may involve fallbacks" [^1].

Counting back 265 commits from the census date lands exactly on the parentless root commit `170a3d8a`, dated 2026-07-13T12:22:21Z, message "feat: scaffold oh-my-cli with toolchain, tools, and fake-provider smoke test" [^33].

That root commit is a single +3,222 / −0 drop landing 39 minutes after the repository was created, already containing a layered CLI plus tests — and roughly 2,093 of those lines are a lockfile, leaving about 1,129 authored lines [^33].
Then the contributor list, which is where the framing breaks. GitHub records 463 contributions from `qwen-code-dev-bot` and 13 from a human account, `qqqys` [^31].
Commit `59eca7c` was authored and committed by qqqys (qys177@gmail.com) at 2026-07-23T07:26:00Z — squarely inside the claimed window.
No agent work commit is cryptographically signed; the API reports verification reason "unsigned" on every non-merge commit, while GitHub's own web-flow merge commits are signed [^32].

`oh-my-cli` is Apache-2.0 TypeScript with three runtime dependencies, roughly 130 `*.test.ts` files across unit, integration and smoke suites, LSP and MCP integration, and an Electron desktop shell [^30].

Querying the Hugging Face API for the Qwen organization sorted by last-modified returns no repository containing "3.8"; the most recently modified Qwen repository dates from 2026-07-22, and the highest version present is Qwen3.6 [^44].

Every Max-tier Qwen flagship since Qwen2.5-Max in January 2025 has shipped closed — Qwen2.5-Max, Qwen3-Max-Preview (September 2025), Qwen3.6-Max-Preview (2026-04-20), Qwen3.7-Max (2026-05-20), and Qwen3.8-Max-Preview (2026-07-19) [^46] — and the Hugging Face organization contains no Max-class checkpoint to contradict it [^44,46].
The closed-flagship policy dates to roughly January 2025 [^46], which makes it an eighteen-month, repeatedly reaffirmed commercial posture rather than a three-month experiment.

Two things cut the other way, and both are real. First, Qwen's **non-Max** track delivers: at Qwen3.5, downloadable weights followed the flagship announcement within roughly 8–11 days, and the Hugging Face organization does contain Qwen3.5-397B-A17B along with its FP8 and GPTQ-Int4 variants, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B and Qwen3.5-27B [^44].

Is sixteen days even the impressive quantity? METR is explicit that its metric measures something else — time horizon is "not the length of time AIs can work independently" but "the amount of serial human labor they can replace with a 50% success rate," and the best measured 50% horizon is about 17 hours [^36].

Qwen's precedent is split by **tier**, not by default: small models ship Apache 2.0, but its largest open checkpoints have carried a bespoke Tongyi Qianwen License reading "If you are commercially using the Materials, and your product or service has more than 100 million monthly active users, You shall request a license from Us" — a license that also forbids relicensing and using outputs to improve any other LLM [^45].

For an actual cost anchor there is exactly one first-party production accounting of a large sparse MoE: DeepSeek's Open Source Week disclosure of 226.75 nodes of 8×H800 averaged over 24 hours, where "assuming the leasing cost of one H800 GPU is $2 per hour, the total daily cost amounts to $87,072" against $562,027 of theoretical daily revenue — the famous "545% cost profit margin" [^51].

Independently, LMSYS served DeepSeek V3 on 96 H100s with wide expert parallelism at "a cost of $0.20/1M output tokens, which is about one-fifth the cost of the official DeepSeek Chat API," landing within 5.6% (prefill) and 6.6% (decode) of DeepSeek's own published profile [^52].
FY2026 capital expenditure reached RMB 126,063 million (US$18,275 million), up roughly 50% from about RMB 84.3 billion in FY2025, with RMB 26,887 million spent in the March quarter alone [^59].

Over the same year free cash flow reversed from an inflow of RMB 73.9 billion to an outflow of RMB 46.6 billion while group adjusted EBITA fell 84% year over year to RMB 5,102 million — a swing management attributes to quick commerce *and* cloud infrastructure jointly, so it is not an AI-only number [^59].

Cloud Intelligence revenue was RMB 41,626 million (US$6,035 million) in the quarter ended 2026-03-31, up 38% year over year, with external customer revenue growth accelerating to 40% and AI-related products at roughly 30% of external cloud revenue [^59].

And the tape has run this play before: the US line closed up 4.14% at $127.31 on 2026-08-03 against a $122.25 prior close, ranging $126.13–$129.50 with an intraday high 1.7% above the close, still far below its $192.67 52-week high and well above its June low of $91.99 [^62]

The Federal Register published on 2026-06-10 the Department of Defense's addition of 65 entities to its Section 1260H Chinese Military Companies list, Alibaba Group Holding Limited among them, on a stated basis of indirect SASAC affiliation — not any AI-specific or model-related conduct [^68].

The consequence that bites is Section 805 of the FY2024 NDAA, effective 2026-06-30, barring DoD from entering, renewing or extending contracts directly with listed entities, with an indirect/supply-chain phase following 2027-06-30 [^69].

The default inference scope is **Global**, documented as "any available node, including within and outside China." Restricting execution to the US is opt-in: "Use model names with the `-us` suffix (such as `qwen-plus-us`) to restrict inference to the US." Without the suffix, inference defaults to Global [^72].

Here is the clearest thing that would weaken a "fully shipped" reading: coverage says GA arrived "via Alibaba Cloud's Model Studio APIs" [^3], yet Model Studio's own pricing and text-generation pages still top out at `qwen3.7-max` [^8].
Second, the competitive incentive genuinely changed: Moonshot shipped Kimi K3, a 2.8T open-weight model, on 2026-07-16, three days before Qwen previewed 3.8-Max [^48].

Moonshot shipped Kimi K3 — 2.8 trillion total parameters, reportedly China's largest model — on 2026-07-16, three days before Alibaba previewed Qwen3.8-Max on 2026-07-19, and K3 activates roughly 104B parameters per token against Qwen's 95B, leaving Qwen both smaller in total and slightly sparser [^63].

The commitment itself is first-party and unambiguous. Alibaba's own launch post states that "The model weights will be open-sourced on Hugging Face and ModelScope next week" [^1], and the official @Alibaba_Qwen account names two artifacts rather than one: "Next week, the open weights of Qwen3.8-Max will be released, and Qwen3.8-27B is also going open-weights to meet you all!" [^6].
Anthropic removed its long-context surcharge in March 2026 and now serves the full 1M window at standard pricing [^13].
It also has a short shelf life: Sonnet 5's $2/$10 is introductory pricing through 2026-08-31, stepping to $3/$15 on 1 September in a pre-announced 50% increase [^20][^13].

The section heading reads "10+ Days of Autonomous Coding: Building a Self-Evolving Harness"; the body reports that the result arrived "after approximately 16 days of fully autonomous AI operation," yielding "265 commits, 127 PRs, and 151 issues" [^1].
Prior-generation work found the Qwen2.5 pretraining corpus overlapping MATH-500, AMC and AIME 2024, and a leakage study across 35 open models ranked the Qwen family highest [^26].
